claim: MetaTrader’s Stochastic handle is built from five calculation inputs: %K period, %D period, slowing, a moving-average method, and a price-field choice.
how_to_test: Rebuild iStochastic-equivalent series for the same symbol/timeframe while varying one input at a time and compare buffers to a known MT5 export.

claim: MQL5 can compute Stochastic either from Low/High prices (STO_LOWHIGH) or from Close/Close prices (STO_CLOSECLOSE).
how_to_test: Compare a Low/High stochastic to a Close/Close stochastic on the same bars; the two series should differ whenever highs and lows extend beyond the closes.

timestamp_or_locator: Key Takeaways; section “Using Stochastic Oscillator to Spot Market Trends”
claim: The stochastic oscillator is bounded between 0 and 100. The page’s traditional reading treats values above 80 as overbought and values below 20 as oversold, and it warns that strong trends can stay in those zones for a long time.
how_to_test: On historical bars, flag %K crossings of 80 and 20 and measure subsequent returns versus a no-signal baseline; report n and do not call an edge below n=30.

timestamp_or_locator: Section “Step-by-Step Guide to Calculating the Stochastic Oscillator”
claim: %K places the latest close inside the period’s high–low range, scaled by 100. The page describes %D as a moving average of %K (it uses a 3-period average in that explanation) and treats a %K/%D cross as a momentum-shift signal.
how_to_test: Compute %K from (close−lowest low)/(highest high−lowest low)×100 and %D as a 3-period average of %K; check crosses against a recorded MT5 or TradingView export.

timestamp_or_locator: Section “Step-by-Step Guide to Calculating the Stochastic Oscillator” (slow vs fast note)
claim: On that page, a slowing period of 1 is described as the fast stochastic, and a slowing period of 3 is described as the internal smoothing used by the slow stochastic.
how_to_test: Export MT5 fast (slowing=1) and slow (slowing=3) Stochastic on the same bars and confirm the slow %K is the smoothed version of the fast %K.

timestamp_or_locator: Parameters (ma_period, applied_price); companion example on the Price Constants page uses input RSIperiod=14
claim: MQL5’s RSI handle is defined by an averaging period (ma_period) and an applied price. The official Price Constants example constructs RSI with period 14 on the close.
how_to_test: Compute Wilder RSI(14) on close and compare it to an MT5 iRSI(14, PRICE_CLOSE) export on the same series.

timestamp_or_locator: Parameters (fast_ema_period, slow_ema_period, signal_period, applied_price) and Note (buffers 0=MAIN_LINE, 1=SIGNAL_LINE)
claim: MQL5’s MACD is defined by a fast average period, a slow average period, a signal period that averages their difference, and an applied price. The main line and the signal line are separate buffers.
how_to_test: Rebuild MACD main as EMA(fast)−EMA(slow) on the applied price and the signal as the documented average of that difference; compare both buffers to an MT5 export.

claim: MQL5’s moving-average handle is defined by a period, an optional horizontal shift, a smoothing method (including simple/SMA), and an applied price.
how_to_test: Compute an SMA of the applied price over the stated period and compare it to MT5 iMA with MODE_SMA on the same bars.

claim: For this project the owner specified these MT5 dialog values: SMA 144 on close (red dashed), SMA 77 on close (orange dashed), MACD(12, 26, SMA 1) on close, RSI(14) on close with levels 10/90/50, and Stochastic %K 5, %D 3, slowing 3, Low/High, Simple, with levels 15/85/50. The same item notes the named JPEG hashes were not on disk when the values were written down.
how_to_test: Diff research/cfx/cfx_osc_combo.py and the v7 renderer against those exact parameters; do not treat the parameter choice itself as proof of an edge.

timestamp_or_locator: Section “## v7 — 10 Nov 2026”, subsection “### Oscillator — one pane, variant B” (settings paragraph)
claim: CFX v7 implements Stochastic(5,3,3) Low/High SMA with levels 15/85/50 as the main oscillator line, RSI(14) with levels 10/90/50 as confirmation, MACD(12,26, signal SMA 1) as confirmation, and SMA 144 / SMA 77 on the price pane. Because a signal period of 1 makes the signal equal the main line, confirmation uses the slope of the MACD main line.
how_to_test: Unit-test the combo helper against a short synthetic series and against the committed GC=F snapshot metadata.

timestamp_or_locator: Section “## v7”, table of variants A/B/C under “### Oscillator — one pane, variant B”
claim: Three confirmation rules were compared on GC=F 15m. Variant A (K/D cross from ≤15/≥85 on this or the prior bar, plus RSI turning and MACD slope) produced 0 signals in the 6–10 Nov visible window (245 bars) and 3 signals on the Sep–Nov sample (4525 bars), all 3 against the next-8-bar move (against-move rate 100%, n=3). Variant C (A plus close on the SMA144 side of the signal) produced 0 signals on both windows.
how_to_test: Re-run research/cfx/cfx_osc_combo.py compare_variants on the same GC=F 15m sample and match the table counts. n=3 is below 30, so it is not evidence.

claim: Variant B uses the same cross-plus-RSI-plus-MACD-slope rule as A, except the 15/85 zone may have been touched in the last 3 bars. On the visible 6–10 Nov window it printed 2 buys and 0 sells, both against the next 8 bars. On the Sep–Nov sample it printed 62 signals (39 buy / 23 sell), 25 with the next-8 move and 37 against it, an against-move rate of 59.7%. The log chose B because it was the only variant that actually fired and had the lowest against-move rate among variants that produced signals. The same paragraph states that 59.7% against-move on the next 8 bars is not an edge.
how_to_test: Reproduce collect_combo_dots variant B on the committed sample; report n, with/against counts, and do not promote an edge (n=62 is below 100; the log already calls it research-only).

claim: Under chosen variant B, the visible window had a BUY at 06 Nov 13:15 Africa/Cairo at 4080.10 (next 8 bars: high +2.6 / low −15.8) and a BUY at 10 Nov 10:00 Africa/Cairo at 4127.00 (next 8: high +3.2 / low −38.8). The log says no SELL fired in that 6–10 Nov window, while 23 sells exist on the longer Sep–Nov sample.
how_to_test: Replay the two timestamps on the committed GC=F 15m series and confirm side, price, and next-8 excursions.

claim: The separate pipeline backtest figure carried into v7 is n=83, TP1-or-better 37.35%, average +0.238R after a $0.30 spread, on yfinance GC=F gold futures (not spot XAUUSD). The log says n≥30 so the numbers may be shown, n<100, and this is not an edge.
how_to_test: Re-run the committed CFX trade engine on the same GC=F sample and compare n, hit rate, and average R after the stated spread. Do not claim an edge unless n≥100 and a pre-registered test meets the project’s t>3 rule.

claim: Project rule: never claim an edge from that backtest. Show the numbers at n≥30, and claim an edge only at n≥100 and t>3 after costs.
how_to_test: Not a market hypothesis. Review copy on the chart, dashboard, and any future V7 tab for compliance.

claim: That page defines a BOS as price breaking a prior swing high in an uptrend (a new higher high) or a prior swing low in a downtrend (a new lower low). It describes BOS as trend continuation, not reversal, and says successive BOS events commonly appear inside a trend.
how_to_test: Label swing breaks in the trend direction on historical bars and measure continuation over the next N bars versus random breaks of the same size; report n.

claim: That page defines a CHoCH (also called a market structure shift there) as price breaking a prior swing low during an uptrend, or a prior swing high during a downtrend, and reads it as a potential reversal.
how_to_test: Label first counter-trend swing breaks and measure whether a new opposite-structure sequence follows, versus unmatched breaks; report n.

claim: That glossary defines a liquidity sweep as price trading through an obvious level, filling resting orders, then reversing. Its test: a sweep is a wick through the level with a close back inside; a genuine breakout closes beyond it.
how_to_test: On marked EQH/EQL, PDH/PDL or session extremes, classify wick-through-and-close-back versus body close-through and compare next-bar delivery; report n.

claim: Equal highs or equal lows are two or more highs (or lows) at nearly the same price. The glossary says stops tend to stack behind them because they look like strong support or resistance.
how_to_test: Pair nearby swing highs/lows under a stated tolerance and measure how often price later trades through the cluster; report n.

claim: CFX treats two confirmed swing highs (or lows) as equal when their prices differ by no more than 0.10 times the current ATR. A later trade beyond that clustered level is recorded as a sweep of the EQH or EQL.
how_to_test: Unit-test find_eq on synthetic equal and unequal swings, then count EQH/EQL sweeps on the committed GC=F window.

timestamp_or_locator: Section “How to read this category” (FVG and order-block summary) plus lesson title “Fair Value Gap (FVG) Explained”
claim: On that page a fair value gap is a three-candle pattern in which the first candle’s high and the third candle’s low do not overlap. Traders watch the gap as an area price may revisit.
how_to_test: Detect three-candle gaps with no wick overlap between candles 1 and 3; measure how often price later trades through the gap. The same page’s own daily-gap fill table is a separate dataset and was not reused as our result.

claim: The page titles an inverse fair value gap as a gap that has been closed through and then acts in the opposite direction.
how_to_test: After a detected FVG is fully traded through, mark it inverted and measure reactions on the first revisit from the opposite side; report n.

timestamp_or_locator: Lesson title “Order Blocks” and section “How to read this category”
claim: That page describes an order block as the last opposite (opposing) candle before a move that breaks structure / a strong move.
how_to_test: After a structure break, box the last opposite candle and measure first-return reactions versus equally sized random candles; report n.

claim: That page titles a breaker block as a failed order block that flips role on the retest.
how_to_test: When price closes through a previously marked order block after a sweep, treat the box as a breaker and measure the first retest from the other side; report n.

timestamp_or_locator: Lesson title “Premium, Discount and Equilibrium” and section “How to read this category”
claim: Premium, discount and equilibrium are described there as splitting a range at 50% to locate cheap and expensive prices.
how_to_test: For each dealing range, mark the 50% equilibrium and compare long setups originating below it versus above it (and the reverse for shorts); report n.

claim: The glossary splits the current dealing range at 50% (equilibrium): above is premium (expensive), below is discount (cheap). It says to look for buys in discount and sells in premium, as a filter that disqualifies zones rather than creating trades by itself.
how_to_test: Filter the same POI set by premium vs discount and compare hit rate and average R; report n.

claim: That page titles optimal trade entry as the 62%–79% retracement zone and the 70.5% level.
how_to_test: On displacement legs, mark retracements into 0.62–0.79 (and the 0.705 line) and measure next-leg continuation versus retracements that stop before 0.62; report n.

claim: The glossary describes OTE as the 62%–79% retracement of an impulse leg, measured with a Fibonacci tool, and says it is used to refine an entry inside a zone rather than as a standalone signal.
how_to_test: Compare OTE-only entries with OTE that also overlaps an FVG or order block; report n for each bucket.

claim: CFX implements OTE as the interval OTE = (0.62, 0.79) with a location flag in_ote, and it draws the 0.705 and 0.79 levels dotted on the latest impulse.
how_to_test: On a known impulse, confirm in_ote is true only while the retracement is inside 0.62–0.79 and that 0.705 / 0.79 levels are emitted.

timestamp_or_locator: Section “What Is ICT CISD (Change in State of Delivery)?” and “The Mechanical Rule — Opening Price, Body Close”
claim: That article defines CISD as a candle body closing beyond the opening price of the consecutive candle series that delivered price into a swept liquidity level. Bullish: body close above the opening of the down-close candles that made the low. Bearish: body close below the opening of the up-close candles that made the high. It says a wick through the level that closes back does not count, and that CISD is a candle-level event that can fire before a swing-based CHoCH.
how_to_test: After a documented sweep, mark the first open of the final same-color delivery run and require a later body close through that open; compare markout versus unmatched sweeps. Do not reuse the article’s NQ/EURUSD walkthrough prices as our data.

timestamp_or_locator: Section “Chart content & style”, item 13, and section “SMC / ICT structure”, items 22–24
claim: In CFX, CISD is drawn as a short origin-to-confirm line on its own candle span, tagged CISD 15m or CISD 4H (including HTF CISD on the lower-timeframe chart). BOS and CHoCH are required as short labeled lines at the broken swing, distinct from each other, not text-only tags.
how_to_test: Visual/regression check of the committed v7 chart and dashboard overlays against those drawing rules. Not a profitability claim.

claim: SMT (smart money technique) divergence is defined there as two correlated instruments disagreeing at a sweep: one makes a new low (or high) and the other refuses. The page reads that break in correlation as a reason to treat the sweep as more likely manipulation than trend, and it lists example pairs EURUSD vs GBPUSD, NQ vs ES, and gold vs silver.
how_to_test: At gold sweep bars, compare a correlated series (the project’s code uses DXY; this glossary example uses silver) and measure reversal rate when the second market fails to confirm the new extreme versus when both confirm; report n.

timestamp_or_locator: SMT helper notes “Gold HH not confirmed by DXY HH” and “Gold LL not confirmed by DXY LL”
claim: This project’s SMT check on the gold chart looks for a gold higher-high or lower-low that is not confirmed by the corresponding DXY higher-high or lower-low.
how_to_test: Replay detect-SMT on the committed window with GC=F and DXY and list the bars that match those notes.

claim: CRT treats every candle as a range. The glossary says that when price sweeps one side of a higher-timeframe candle’s range and closes back inside, it tends to deliver to the other side. Its validity rule: wick raid plus close inside may be traded as manipulation; a body close beyond the range is treated as a genuine breakout and is not faded.
how_to_test: On closed 4H (or Daily) candles, mark next-candle sweeps that close back inside versus body breaks, and measure delivery toward the opposite extreme; report n.

timestamp_or_locator: Section “Forex Market Hours”, summer table (Early April to early October) and winter table (November to mid-March)
claim: BabyPips publishes city-session clocks in New York time. In the summer table: Tokyo 8:00 pm–5:00 am ET, London 3:00 am–12:00 pm ET, New York 8:00 am–5:00 pm ET. In the winter table: Tokyo 7:00 pm–4:00 am ET, London 3:00 am–12:00 pm ET, New York 8:00 am–5:00 pm ET. The page also says the London–New York overlap is usually 8:00 am–12:00 pm ET and is typically the busiest stretch, and that DST changeover weeks can shift clocks by an hour.

claim: This project’s XPIX 15-minute and 1-hour levels are taken from the latest completed 15-minute and 1-hour bar high and low. The helper hides a level when price is more than 15 ATR from both the high and the low. This is an implementation detail of CFX/XPIX, not an external textbook named “XPIX levels”.

These are display requirements, not a claim that each concept has a measured edge.

timestamp_or_locator: Function detect_fvgs (three-bar comparison of low[i] vs high[i-2] and high[i] vs low[i-2]) and function detect_ifvg
claim: CFX detects a bullish FVG when the current low is above the high of two bars earlier by at least 0.30 ATR, and a bearish FVG when the current high is below the low of two bars earlier by the same minimum. An IFVG is recorded when a previously detected FVG is filled and later reclaimed, flipping the zone’s side.
how_to_test: Unit-test detect_fvgs / detect_ifvg on synthetic three-bar gaps and on the committed GC=F window; compare counts with the dashboard export.
